 Energy Association Urges Pennsylvanians Struggling With Heating Bills to Apply Now for LIHEAP Assistance
 By Editor - November 10, 2026 0 2 Facebook Twitter Linkedin Email The Energy Association of Pennsylvania, which represents 18 utility providers across the commonwealth, today reminded residents that the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) is now accepting applications for the 2026-27 heating season.
 The federally funded program, which opened Monday, Nov. 2, provides financial assistance to eligible households struggling to pay their heating bills. LIHEAP offers direct cash grants, as well as crisis grants for households in immediate danger of being without heat.
 “As temperatures begin to fall, we want Pennsylvania families to know that help is available to keep their homes warm and safe this winter,” said EAP President and CEO Andy Tubbs. “We encourage anyone who may be struggling with their energy bills to apply for LIHEAP and contact their utility provider to learn about other assistance programs. The sooner customers seek help, the more options may be available to them.”
 LIHEAP cash grants range from $200 to $1,000, depending on household size, income and fuel type. Grants are paid directly to the utility company or fuel provider and credited to the customer’s account. Eligible households do not have to repay the assistance. Applications will be accepted through April 23, 2027.
 Pennsylvania residents seeking LIHEAP assistance or additional information can contact:
 Their utility provider:   Pennsylvania utilities offer a variety of customer assistance programs, payment arrangements and energy-saving resources. EAP’s Be Energy Wise website, weatherizemyhome.org , provides utility contact information and additional resources.
 Pennsylvania Department of Human Services:   Residents can learn more about LIHEAP, eligibility requirements and how to apply at https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dhs/resources/liheap or by calling 1-866-857-7095 . 
 “Nobody should wait until they’re facing a heating emergency to ask for assistance,” Tubbs said. “Pennsylvania’s utilities are committed to working with customers to help them manage their energy costs and maintain essential service throughout the winter.”
